body: Not sure if this should be "core" or "infrastructure", so leaving that label off for now.
I'd like to work on this one if it gets accepted :)
The rule should throw if it uses `fix` and doesn't have `fixable` set. If that isn't happening, then that's a bug we should fix. That would, in turn, throw an error during testing.
It's not throwing in the current implementation. It will just not run fix on the rule that doesn't have `meta.fixable` set.
@ilyavolodin then we should throw in that case. I think we talked about this way back, so easy to forget.
I think throwing is fine. We just need to make sure the code is done in such a way that it would only through for rules in new format.

issue.title: Fix: throw when rule uses `fix` but `meta.fixable` not set (fixes #5970)
